branch: Indian Army
theater_or_location: Zoji La Pass, Dras, and Kargil sectors (Jammu & Kashmir)
operational_objective: Break the siege of Leh, clear Pakistani raiders and regular forces from high mountain passes, and reconnect Srinagar with Ladakh
adversary_or_context: Pakistani regular troops and tribal militia invaders during the First Indo-Pak War (1947–1948)
key_commanders_and_units: Lt. Gen. K. M. Cariappa, Maj. Gen. K. S. Thimayya; 77 Para Brigade, 1st Cavalry (Stuart Light Tanks), 1 Patiala
key_assets_and_platforms: M3 Stuart light tanks dismantled and hauled up to high altitudes, 25-pounder field guns
tactical_execution: Surprise tactical deployment of Stuart light tanks across rough tracks at an unprecedented altitude of 11,578 feet, breaking fortified enemy bunker positions at Zoji La
outcome_and_strategic_result: Recapture of Zoji La, Dras, and Kargil, securing the overland axis to Leh and permanently retaining the Ladakh region within the Indian Union
honors_and_decorations: Maha Vir Chakra awarded to key unit commanders; landmark high-altitude armor battle in military history

branch: Joint (Indian Army supported by Royal Indian Air Force)
theater_or_location: Hyderabad Princely State
operational_objective: Integrate the recalcitrant Princely State of Hyderabad into the Indian Union and dismantle the Razakar private militia
adversary_or_context: Hyderabad State Forces and the armed communal paramilitary Razakars commanded by Kasim Razvi under Nizam Mir Osman Ali Khan
key_commanders_and_units: Lt. Gen. Eric Goddard (Southern Command), Maj. Gen. J. N. Chaudhuri (1 Armoured Division); 7th Infantry Brigade
key_assets_and_platforms: Sherman tanks, Humber and Stuart armored cars, Hawker Tempest aircraft (RIAF)
tactical_execution: Two-pronged coordinated armored thrust from the western axis (Sholapur) and eastern axis (Vijayawada), encircling the state capital within 100 hours
outcome_and_strategic_result: Unconditional surrender of the Nizam's military on September 17; formal accession of Hyderabad State to India and appointment of Maj. Gen. Chaudhuri as Military Governor
honors_and_decorations: Ashoka Chakra awarded to Havildar Bachittar Singh and Naik Narbahadur Thapa (first recipients)

branch: Tri-Service (Indian Army, Indian Navy, Indian Air Force)
theater_or_location: Goa, Daman, and Diu (Portuguese India)
operational_objective: Liberate the colonial Portuguese enclaves of Goa, Daman, and Diu and integrate them into mainland India
adversary_or_context: Portuguese Armed Forces and Portuguese Navy under Governor-General Manuel António Vassalo e Silva
key_commanders_and_units: Lt. Gen. J. N. Chaudhuri (Southern Command), Maj. Gen. K. P. Candeth (17 Infantry Division), Rear Adm. B. S. Soman; INS Delhi, INS Trishul
key_assets_and_platforms: INS Vikrant carrier air wing, INS Mysore, INS Betwa, Canberras and Hunters (IAF), Centurion and AMX-13 tanks
tactical_execution: Simultaneous tri-service operations: naval surface gunfire sinking the Portuguese sloop NRP Afonso de Albuquerque, air strikes disabling Dabolim airstrip, and rapid multi-axis ground advances
outcome_and_strategic_result: Decisive victory in 36 hours; Portuguese signed instrument of surrender, ending 451 years of Portuguese colonial rule in India; territories integrated as Union Territories
honors_and_decorations: Param Vir Chakra awarded posthumously to Captain P. K. Sehgal; multiple Vir Chakras

branch: Indian Army supported by Indian Air Force
theater_or_location: Lahore Sector, Punjab (Western Border)
operational_objective: Relieve Pakistani offensive pressure on Akhnoor/Chhamb (Operation Grand Slam) by opening a major multi-division counter-offensive across the international border toward Lahore
adversary_or_context: Pakistan Army (10 and 11 Divisions, 1st Armoured Division) during the Second Indo-Pak War
key_commanders_and_units: Lt. Gen. Harbaksh Singh (Western Command), Maj. Gen. Joginder Singh (XI Corps); 3 Jat, 15 Infantry Division
key_assets_and_platforms: Centurion and Sherman tanks, 25-pounder guns, Mystère and Hunter fighter jets
tactical_execution: Simultaneous crossing of the International Border along three main axes (Amritsar-Lahore, Khalra-Burki, and Khem Karan), advancing to the Ichhogil Canal and capturing Dograi
outcome_and_strategic_result: Forced Pakistan to divert its primary armored divisions from Jammu and Kashmir, establishing Indian defensive parity along the Ichhogil Canal until the UN ceasefire
honors_and_decorations: Maha Vir Chakra awarded to Lt. Col. Desmond Hayde (CO, 3 Jat) for the assault on Dograi

branch: Indian Army
theater_or_location: Sialkot Sector, Shakargarh Bulge (Punjab/J&K border)
operational_objective: Pin down and destroy Pakistan's premier strike formation (6th Armoured Division) and cut off the Sialkot-Lahore rail and road communication links
adversary_or_context: Pakistan Army I Corps and 6th Armoured Division equipped with US-supplied M48 Patton tanks
key_commanders_and_units: Lt. Gen. P. O. Dunn (I Corps), Maj. Gen. Rajindar Singh 'Sparrow' (1 Armoured Division); 16 Cavalry, Poona Horse
key_assets_and_platforms: Centurion Mk VII tanks, Sherman tanks, AMX-13 tanks
tactical_execution: Massive armored advance leading to the Battle of Phillora and the Battle of Chawinda, involving direct tank-on-tank duels across expansive plains
outcome_and_strategic_result: Severe attrition of Pakistani armor at Phillora, blunting Pakistan's armored offensive capability in the western theater
honors_and_decorations: Maha Vir Chakra awarded to Maj. Gen. Rajindar Singh 'Sparrow' and Lt. Col. A. B. Tarapore (later awarded PVC posthumously)

branch: Indian Army supported by Indian Air Force
theater_or_location: Asal Uttar, Khem Karan Sector, Punjab
operational_objective: Halt and encircle the advance of Pakistan's 1st Armoured Division aiming to capture the bridges over the Beas river and encircle Indian forces in Punjab
adversary_or_context: Pakistan Army 1st Armoured Division and 11th Infantry Division deploying superior M47 and M48 Patton tanks
key_commanders_and_units: Lt. Gen. Harbaksh Singh, Maj. Gen. Gurbaksh Singh (4 Mountain Division), Brig. K. K. Singh; 9 Deccan Horse, 3 Rajputana Rifles
key_assets_and_platforms: Centurion and AMX-13 tanks, recoilless (RCL) guns mounted on jeeps
tactical_execution: Indian forces formed a horseshoe defensive perimeter and breached the Rohi Nullah canal to flood sugarcane fields, trapping advancing Patton tanks in the mud for close-range ambush
outcome_and_strategic_result: Decisive Indian victory; over 95 Pakistani tanks were destroyed or captured intact ('Patton Nagar'), breaking Pakistan's strategic armor strike capability
honors_and_decorations: Param Vir Chakra awarded posthumously to Company Quartermaster Havildar Abdul Hamid for destroying multiple Patton tanks with an RCL gun

operation_name: Nathu La and Cho La Clashes
branch: Indian Army
theater_or_location: Nathu La and Cho La Passes, Sikkim Border
operational_objective: Fortify and lay border fencing along the watershed demarcation at Nathu La and defend sovereign Himalayan passes against Chinese incursions
adversary_or_context: Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA)
key_commanders_and_units: Lt. Gen. Sagat Singh (GOC 17 Mountain Division); 2 Grenadiers, 18 Rajput, 7/11 Gorkha Rifles
key_assets_and_platforms: Artillery batteries, medium machine guns, high-altitude defensive bunkers
tactical_execution: When PLA forces opened machine-gun fire on Indian troops laying wire, Indian artillery launched heavy counter-battery fire from dominant ridge positions, devastating Chinese command posts
outcome_and_strategic_result: Decisive Indian tactical victory; heavy Chinese casualties and destruction of PLA fortifications, checking Chinese aggression along the Sikkim frontier
honors_and_decorations: Maha Vir Chakra awarded to Lt. Col. Rai Singh and posthumously to Capt. P. S. Dagar; multiple Vir Chakras

branch: Indian Army in coordination with Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) and State Police
theater_or_location: Red Corridor junction (West Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa borders)
operational_objective: Sanitize and cordon border regions to suppress the violent insurgent infrastructure of the first-phase Naxalite movement
adversary_or_context: Communist Party of India (Marxist-Leninist) insurgent armed squads led by Charu Majumdar and Kanu Sanyal
key_commanders_and_units: Lt. Gen. J. S. Aurora (Eastern Command); Indian Army infantry brigades alongside state armed police
key_assets_and_platforms: Cordon-and-search gear, light troop transports, paramilitary combing units
tactical_execution: The Army formed outer concentric cordons around suspected forest belts and towns while the police and CRPF conducted inner search-and-arrest operations
outcome_and_strategic_result: Disrupted the early rural and urban network of the Naxalite insurgency, stabilizing the border rear before the 1971 Bangladesh Liberation War
honors_and_decorations: Internal security citation awards and state police medals

branch: Indian Air Force and Indian Army
theater_or_location: Boyra salient, East Pakistan border (West Bengal)
operational_objective: Intercept and shoot down Pakistan Air Force jets violating Indian airspace while supporting allied Mukti Bahini positions
adversary_or_context: Pakistan Air Force (No. 14 Squadron 'Tail Choppers') deploying Canadair Sabre Mk 6 fighters
key_commanders_and_units: No. 22 Squadron IAF ('Swifts') based at Dum Dum; Flight Lieutenants Roy Massey, M. A. Ganapathy, Donald Lazarus, Sunith Soares
key_assets_and_platforms: Folland Gnat lightweight fighter aircraft
tactical_execution: Four Gnats scrambled in response to low-level PAF Sabre incursions over the Boyra peninsula; engaged in close-range dogfights, shooting down three PAF Sabres in minutes
outcome_and_strategic_result: First direct air-to-air combat encounter preceding the formal outbreak of the 1971 war; demonstrated the aerial combat superiority of the indigenous Gnat ('Sabre Slayer')
honors_and_decorations: Vir Chakras awarded to all participating IAF fighter pilots

branch: Tri-Service (Indian Army, Navy, Air Force) with Mukti Bahini
theater_or_location: East Pakistan (now Bangladesh)
operational_objective: Liberate East Pakistan, dismantle Pakistani military occupation, and establish the independent sovereign nation of Bangladesh
adversary_or_context: Pakistan Eastern Military Command under Lt. Gen. A. A. K. Niazi
key_commanders_and_units: Gen. Sam Manekshaw (COAS), Lt. Gen. J. S. Aurora (Eastern Command), Maj. Gen. J. F. R. Jacob; IV, XXXIII, and II Corps
key_assets_and_platforms: PT-76 amphibious tanks, Mi-4 helicopters, MiG-21FL, Hunter, and Su-7 aircraft, INS Vikrant
tactical_execution: Multi-pronged blitzkrieg bypassing fortified Pakistani strongpoints ('hedgehog defense'), crossing major river obstacles, and converging rapidly on Dacca
outcome_and_strategic_result: Historic liberation of Bangladesh; unconditional surrender of 93,000 Pakistani soldiers on December 16, 1971, the largest public military surrender since World War II
honors_and_decorations: Param Vir Chakra awarded to Lance Naik Albert Ekka; Field Marshal rank bestowed on Sam Manekshaw

branch: Indian Navy
theater_or_location: Karachi Port and Arabian Sea (Pakistan)
operational_objective: Launch a nighttime anti-ship missile assault on the naval headquarters and primary anchorage of the Pakistan Navy at Karachi
adversary_or_context: Pakistan Navy surface combatants and coastal defenses
key_commanders_and_units: Adm. S. M. Nanda, Vice Adm. S. N. Kohli, Cdr. B. B. Yadav (25th Missile Boat Squadron); INS Nipat, INS Nirghat, INS Veer, INS Kiltan
key_assets_and_platforms: Osa-I class missile boats armed with Soviet-origin SS-N-2B Styx anti-ship missiles, Petya-class corvettes
tactical_execution: High-speed night ingress toward Karachi; fired Styx anti-ship missiles at long range, sinking the destroyer PNS Khaibar, minesweeper PNS Muhafiz, and a merchant ship, while setting the Kemari oil storage tanks ablaze
outcome_and_strategic_result: Crippled Pakistan's naval operational capabilities on the western seaboard with zero Indian naval casualties; commemorated annually as Indian Navy Day on December 4
honors_and_decorations: Maha Vir Chakra awarded to Cdr. B. B. Yadav and Lt. Cdr. B. N. Kavina

branch: Indian Navy
theater_or_location: Karachi approaches, Arabian Sea
operational_objective: Deliver a follow-up naval missile strike on Karachi harbor to finish off damaged surface vessels and enforce an absolute maritime blockade
adversary_or_context: Pakistan Navy shore batteries and remaining surface fleet
key_commanders_and_units: Cdr. K. M. V. Nair; INS Vinash (Missile boat), INS Trishul, INS Talwar (Frigates)
key_assets_and_platforms: Osa-class missile boat, SS-N-2B Styx missiles, Type 12 frigates
tactical_execution: Penetrated rough seas and coastal patrol lines; INS Vinash launched four Styx missiles, sinking the merchant ship SS Harmattan and naval tanker PNS Dacca, while damaging shore fuel reserves
outcome_and_strategic_result: Total paralysis of Karachi port operations; merchant shipping refused to dock, choking Pakistan's sea trade and fuel supplies for the remainder of the war
honors_and_decorations: Maha Vir Chakra awarded to Lt. Cdr. Vijai Jerath (Commanding Officer, INS Vinash)

branch: Indian Army and Indian Air Force
theater_or_location: Tangail, East Pakistan
operational_objective: Air-drop an airborne battalion combat team behind enemy lines to capture the Poongli Bridge over the Jamuna River and cut off retreating Pakistani forces
adversary_or_context: Pakistan Army 93rd Infantry Brigade retreating toward Dacca
key_commanders_and_units: Lt. Col. K. S. Pannu; 2nd Battalion, The Parachute Regiment (2 Para), supported by IAF transport squadrons
key_assets_and_platforms: An-12, C-119 Packet, and Dakota transport aircraft, Para field artillery guns
tactical_execution: Flawless daytime airborne drop of over 700 paratroopers and artillery; 2 Para secured Poongli bridge within hours, linking up with Kaderia rebel fighters and routing Pakistani columns
outcome_and_strategic_result: Completely severed the retreat of Pakistani forces to Dacca, accelerating the fall of the capital and the surrender
honors_and_decorations: Maha Vir Chakra awarded to Lt. Col. K. S. Pannu; Battle Honour 'Poongli Bridge'

branch: Indian Army and Indian Air Force
theater_or_location: Meghna River, Ashuganj-Bhairab Bazar sector (East Pakistan)
operational_objective: Bypass blown bridges over the wide Meghna River to air-land infantry directly on the road to Dacca
adversary_or_context: Pakistani 14th Infantry Division entrenched at Bhairab Bazar
key_commanders_and_units: Lt. Gen. Sagat Singh (IV Corps), Group Captain Chandan Singh (IAF); 311 Infantry Brigade
key_assets_and_platforms: Mi-4 transport helicopters, PT-76 amphibious tanks, IAF escort fighters
tactical_execution: Continuous day-and-night helicopter airlift across the unbridged, mile-wide river, transporting thousands of troops and tons of equipment past heavy enemy positions
outcome_and_strategic_result: Outmaneuvered Pakistani defensive lines, allowing Indian troops to advance to the outskirts of Dacca without meeting major resistance
honors_and_decorations: Maha Vir Chakra awarded to Group Captain Chandan Singh for air operations under fire

branch: Indian Army and Indian Air Force
theater_or_location: Longewala border post, Thar Desert, Rajasthan
operational_objective: Hold the isolated desert border post against an armored and mechanized infantry assault until air and ground reinforcements arrived
adversary_or_context: Pakistan Army 51st Infantry Brigade and 22nd Cavalry (40+ Sherman and T-59 tanks)
key_commanders_and_units: Maj. Kuldip Singh Chandpuri (23 Punjab), Wing Cdr. M. S. Bawa (Jaisalmer IAF Base); Hunters of No. 122 Squadron
key_assets_and_platforms: Jeep-mounted 106mm RCL guns, Hawker Hunter ground-attack fighters
tactical_execution: A company of 120 soldiers held the sand dunes overnight using anti-tank minefields and RCL fire; at dawn, IAF Hunters systematically eliminated Pakistani armor stuck in the sand
outcome_and_strategic_result: Decisive Indian victory; over 36 Pakistani tanks and scores of vehicles destroyed, aborting Pakistan's western offensive in the desert
honors_and_decorations: Maha Vir Chakra awarded to Maj. Kuldip Singh Chandpuri; landmark anti-armor defensive stand

branch: Indian Army
theater_or_location: Basantar River, Shakargarh Bulge (Punjab/J&K border)
operational_objective: Establish a secure bridgehead across the minefield-infested Basantar River and neutralize Pakistan's 8th Armoured Brigade
adversary_or_context: Pakistan Army 8th Armoured Brigade and elite mechanized formations
key_commanders_and_units: Lt. Gen. K. K. Singh (I Corps); 17 Poona Horse, 4 Horse, 16 Madras, 3 Grenadiers
key_assets_and_platforms: Centurion tanks, T-55 tanks, combat engineer mine-clearing trawls
tactical_execution: Engineers cleared minefields under direct enemy fire, allowing Centurion tanks to push through and defeat waves of Patton counter-attacks in intense close-range tank duels
outcome_and_strategic_result: Destruction of 46 Pakistani tanks, securing the Shakargarh bulge and shielding the vital Jammu-Pathankot highway from disruption
honors_and_decorations: Param Vir Chakra awarded to 2nd Lt. Arun Khetarpal (posthumously) and Major Hoshiar Singh; one of the most decorated engagements in Indian military history

branch: Indian Army
theater_or_location: Gangtok, Sikkim
operational_objective: Disarm the palace royal guard of the Chogyal of Sikkim to protect democratic representatives and maintain border security
adversary_or_context: Royal Sikkim Guards resisting integration with the Indian Union
key_commanders_and_units: Indian Army Eastern Command forces
key_assets_and_platforms: Light infantry armored convoys, tactical communications networks
tactical_execution: Swift cordon of the royal palace at Gangtok, disarming the 400-strong palace guards in under an hour without major civilian casualties
outcome_and_strategic_result: A referendum followed where 97.5% voted to abolish the monarchy; the 36th Constitutional Amendment made Sikkim the 22nd state of the Indian Union
honors_and_decorations: Administrative commendations; key geopolitical integration of the vital Siliguri Corridor flank

branch: Indian Army supported by Central Paramilitary Forces
theater_or_location: Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple) complex, Amritsar, Punjab
operational_objective: Remove heavily armed Sikh separatist militants led by Jarnail Singh Bhindranwale from the Golden Temple complex
adversary_or_context: Armed Sikh militants entrenched in fortified pillboxes under the tactical leadership of former Maj. Gen. Shabeg Singh
key_commanders_and_units: Lt. Gen. K. Sundarji (Western Command), Lt. Gen. R. S. Dyal, Maj. Gen. K. S. Brar (9 Infantry Division); 1 Para Commando, 10 Guards
key_assets_and_platforms: Vijayanta main battle tanks, BMP-1 infantry fighting vehicles, Carl Gustaf rocket launchers
tactical_execution: Night infantry assault meeting heavy machine-gun and RPG fire from the Akal Takht; Vijayanta tanks were brought into the Parikrama to neutralize fortified basement bunkers
outcome_and_strategic_result: Elimination of the militant leadership and recovery of large arms caches; caused heavy casualties, structural damage, and deep political fallout
honors_and_decorations: Multiple gallantry decorations awarded amidst contentious political controversy

branch: Indian Army and Paramilitary Forces
theater_or_location: Rural and border districts of Punjab
operational_objective: Prevent widespread rural civil armed insurrection and seal the international border with Pakistan following Operation Blue Star
adversary_or_context: Dispersed insurgent networks, sleeper cells, and armed fringe elements in rural Punjab
key_commanders_and_units: Lt. Gen. K. Sundarji; multiple infantry divisions deployed across Punjab's border belt
key_assets_and_platforms: Motorized infantry patrols, riverine surveillance crafts, border watchtowers
tactical_execution: Broad cordon-and-search operations across gurudwaras, villages, and border areas, detaining suspected cadres and establishing checkpoints
outcome_and_strategic_result: Suppressed immediate retaliatory rural uprisings, but exacerbated local grievances, shifting militancy into a prolonged asymmetric phase
honors_and_decorations: Internal security deployment medals

branch: Joint (Indian Army and Indian Air Force)
theater_or_location: Siachen Glacier, Saltoro Ridge (Karakoram Range, Ladakh)
operational_objective: Pre-empt Pakistan's planned Operation Ababeel to seize the unoccupied Siachen Glacier and dominating peaks along the Saltoro Ridge
adversary_or_context: Pakistan Army Special Services Group (SSG) and Northern Light Infantry
key_commanders_and_units: Lt. Gen. P. N. Hoon (XV Corps), Maj. Gen. Shiv Sharma; Kumaon Regiment, Ladakh Scouts; IAF No. 114 Helicopter Unit ('Siachen Pioneers')
key_assets_and_platforms: Mi-8, Cheetah, and Chetak helicopters, An-12 and IL-76 transports, specialized high-altitude gear
tactical_execution: Airlifted troops onto the glacier using helicopters, occupying the key passes of Sia La, Bilafond La, and Gyong La on the Saltoro Ridge days ahead of Pakistan
outcome_and_strategic_result: Secured Indian control over the entire 76 km Siachen Glacier and dominating heights of Saltoro Ridge, creating the world's highest battlefield
honors_and_decorations: Maha Vir Chakra awarded to Major (later Lt. Gen.) Sanjay Kulkarni; operational framework continues to date

branch: Indian Army and State Police Forces
theater_or_location: Terai foothills (Uttar Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, Madhya Pradesh)
operational_objective: Track, isolate, and dismantle Sikh extremist logistics lines, safehouses, and training camps established outside the borders of Punjab
adversary_or_context: Militant splinter groups fleeing Punjab looking to establish transit sanctuaries across North Indian states
key_commanders_and_units: Central Command and Western Command infantry units in liaison with state police intelligence
key_assets_and_platforms: Mobile search columns, intelligence interception cells
tactical_execution: Coordinated intelligence-led cordon operations across the Terai forest belt, arresting key organizers and seizing weapons consignments
outcome_and_strategic_result: Prevented the expansion of insurgent logistics hubs outside Punjab, containing the operational footprint of the militancy
honors_and_decorations: Police and Army operational commendation cards

branch: Tri-Service (Indian Army, Navy, and Air Force)
theater_or_location: Thar Desert, Rajasthan (near the Pakistan border)
operational_objective: Conduct the largest mechanized mobilization exercise in South Asia to test integrated strike doctrines, amphibious assault, and electronic warfare capabilities
adversary_or_context: Deterrence demonstration against Pakistan during peak cross-border militancy support in Punjab
key_commanders_and_units: Gen. K. Sundarji (COAS), Lt. Gen. P. N. Hoon; nearly 500,000 troops, multiple Strike Corps
key_assets_and_platforms: T-72 main battle tanks, BMP-2 IFVs, mechanized artillery, IAF ground-attack fighters
tactical_execution: Simulated deep mechanized thrusts, computerized electronic warfare, and real-time command-and-control maneuvers near the international border
outcome_and_strategic_result: Triggered counter-mobilization by the Pakistan Army, bringing both nations close to open conflict; defused via diplomatic hotlines and de-escalation agreements
honors_and_decorations: Established the doctrine of modern integrated mechanized warfare in the subcontinent

branch: Indian Air Force
theater_or_location: Jaffna peninsula, Northern Sri Lanka
operational_objective: Airdrop humanitarian food supplies over besieged Jaffna to relieve the population and deliver a diplomatic warning against the Sri Lankan Army's Operation Vadamarachchi
adversary_or_context: Sri Lankan Armed Forces surrounding Jaffna; conducted without clearance from Sri Lankan air traffic control
key_commanders_and_units: Air Marshal S. Raghavendran (Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Southern Air Command); No. 33 Squadron IAF
key_assets_and_platforms: Five An-32 transport aircraft escorted by four Mirage 2000 multi-role fighters carrying Matra Super 530D missiles
tactical_execution: Mirage 2000s escorted An-32 transports across the Palk Strait, carrying out low-altitude drops of 25 tons of relief supplies over Jaffna without encountering aerial challenge
outcome_and_strategic_result: Halted the Sri Lankan military offensive, compelling President J. R. Jayewardene to negotiate the Indo-Sri Lanka Accord and invite the Indian Peace Keeping Force (IPKF)
honors_and_decorations: Vayu Sena Medals awarded to transport and escort lead pilots

branch: Indian Army
theater_or_location: Saltoro Ridge, Siachen Glacier (altitude 21,153 feet)
operational_objective: Capture Pakistan's fortified 'Quaid Post' overlooking the Bilafond La pass, which dominated Indian troop movements on the glacier
adversary_or_context: Pakistan Army Special Services Group (SSG) occupying vertical ice cliffs
key_commanders_and_units: Maj. Varinder Singh, Naib Subedar Bana Singh; 8th Battalion, Jammu and Kashmir Light Infantry (8 JAK LI)
key_assets_and_platforms: Rope-climbing gear, ice axes, high-altitude artillery support
tactical_execution: Naib Subedar Bana Singh led an assault team up a 1,500-foot vertical ice wall amid a blizzard, approaching the post from an unexpected route to clear enemy bunkers with hand grenades and bayonets
outcome_and_strategic_result: Successful capture of the highest post on the Saltoro Ridge, neutralizing Pakistani observation lines; the post was renamed 'Bana Top' in his honor
honors_and_decorations: Param Vir Chakra awarded to Naib Subedar Bana Singh; Maha Vir Chakra to 2nd Lt. Rajiv Pande (posthumously)

branch: Joint (Indian Peace Keeping Force - Army, Navy, Air Force)
theater_or_location: Jaffna Peninsula, Northern Sri Lanka
operational_objective: Disarm the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) and gain control of Jaffna town to enforce the Indo-Sri Lanka Accord
adversary_or_context: LTTE insurgent cadres fighting from fortified urban bunkers and minefields
key_commanders_and_units: Lt. Gen. Depinder Singh, Maj. Gen. Harkirat Singh; 54 Air Assault Division, 10 Para Commando, 13 Sikh LI
key_assets_and_platforms: Mi-8 and Mi-25 helicopter gunships, T-72 tanks, BMP-1 IFVs
tactical_execution: Heliborne commando drops on Jaffna University football ground amid heavy sniper fire, followed by room-to-room urban combat and heavy artillery clearing operations
outcome_and_strategic_result: IPKF captured Jaffna city, forcing the LTTE to retreat into the Vanni jungles to wage guerrilla warfare, at a cost of over 1,200 Indian casualties
honors_and_decorations: Param Vir Chakra awarded posthumously to Major Ramaswamy Parameswaran; several Maha Vir Chakras

branch: Assam Rifles and Indian Army
theater_or_location: Oinam and Senapati District, Manipur
operational_objective: Recover stolen arms, ammunition, and sanitize the area following an insurgent attack on the Assam Rifles outpost at Oinam
adversary_or_context: National Socialist Council of Nagaland (NSCN) insurgents
key_commanders_and_units: Assam Rifles and Mountain Division units
key_assets_and_platforms: Counter-insurgency jungle reconnaissance teams, light combat transports
tactical_execution: Intensive counter-insurgency sweep across 30 Naga villages, cordoning hills to capture insurgents and recover lost weapon stockpiles
outcome_and_strategic_result: Recovered most of the looted weapons, but faced domestic and international scrutiny over alleged human rights excesses
honors_and_decorations: Internal counter-insurgency commendations

branch: National Security Guard (NSG) supported by Indian Army and Punjab Police
theater_or_location: Golden Temple Complex, Amritsar, Punjab
operational_objective: Flush out armed Sikh militants occupying the Golden Temple complex without damaging the shrine or entering the Sanctum Sanctorum
adversary_or_context: Armed Khalistani militants belonging to KCF and other factions
key_commanders_and_units: K. P. S. Gill (DGP Punjab Police); NSG 51 Special Action Group (SAG), under overall Army surveillance
key_assets_and_platforms: Heckler & Koch PSG1 sniper rifles, tear gas munitions, floodlights, water and electricity cuts
tactical_execution: Surrounded the complex with expert snipers on water towers; cut off water and food supplies, using sniper fire and psychological pressure until the militants surrendered publicly
outcome_and_strategic_result: Clean surrender of over 90 militants with zero damage to the shrine, avoiding the political fallout of Blue Star and turning public sentiment against the militants
honors_and_decorations: Padma Shri and gallantry medals conferred on key police and commando leaders

branch: Tri-Service (Indian Army, Air Force, and Navy)
theater_or_location: Malé, Maldives and surrounding waters
operational_objective: Thwart a mercenary coup against President Maumoon Abdul Gayoom and restore democratic order in the Maldives
adversary_or_context: 80+ armed mercenaries of the People's Liberation Organisation of Tamil Eelam (PLOTE) backed by Maldivian businessman Abdullah Luthufi
key_commanders_and_units: Brig. Farooq Bulsara; 50th Independent Parachute Brigade (6 Para), No. 44 Squadron IAF, INS Betwa, INS Godavari
key_assets_and_platforms: Il-76 transport aircraft, Type 12 and Godavari-class frigates, Tu-142 maritime patrol planes, Sea King helicopters
tactical_execution: Non-stop night flight of Il-76s landing paratroopers directly onto the unlit Hulhulé airstrip; troops secured the airport, crossed to Malé by boats, rescued the President, and intercepted the fleeing hostage vessel MV Progress Light at sea
outcome_and_strategic_result: Complete victory within 12 hours; neutralized mercenaries, freed hostages, restored the legitimate government, and established India as a net security provider in the Indian Ocean
honors_and_decorations: International acclaim from the US, UK, and UN; multiple Vir Chakras awarded

branch: Indian Army (IPKF)
theater_or_location: Northern and Eastern Provinces, Sri Lanka
operational_objective: Disrupt LTTE supply bases, weapons fabrication units, and forest hideouts following their retreat from Jaffna
adversary_or_context: Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) guerrilla units
key_commanders_and_units: IPKF Sector Commanders; 4 Mountain Division, Para commandos
key_assets_and_platforms: Heliborne search squads, armored personnel carriers, tactical jungle tracking dogs
tactical_execution: Combined tracking operations into the dense scrub jungles of Vavuniya and Mullaitivu to interdict insurgent supply routes
outcome_and_strategic_result: Dismantled improvised mortar-manufacturing factories and recovered weapons, keeping the insurgent cadre on the move
honors_and_decorations: Sena Medals and Mention-in-Despatches for tactical unit officers

branch: Indian Army (IPKF)
theater_or_location: Vadamarachchi sector, Northern Sri Lanka
operational_objective: Isolate and clear LTTE cells attempting to re-infiltrate the populated northern coast of the Jaffna peninsula
adversary_or_context: LTTE local cadres and sea-borne supply boats
key_commanders_and_units: 54 Air Assault Division units alongside naval coastal patrols
key_assets_and_platforms: Inshore patrol vessels, Mi-8 transport choppers, light armored vehicles
tactical_execution: Simultaneous coastal blockades by the Navy and inland sweep operations by infantry, cutting off weapons-smuggling routes across the Palk Strait
outcome_and_strategic_result: Prevented the LTTE from retaking urban Jaffna, stabilizing the area ahead of the North-Eastern Provincial Council elections
honors_and_decorations: Gallantry awards for counter-insurgency patrolling

branch: Indian Army in coordination with Punjab Police
theater_or_location: Rural Punjab and the Indo-Pak border belt
operational_objective: Reclaim control of rural and border areas during the night from heavily armed separatist militants
adversary_or_context: Khalistani insurgent outfits (KCF, KLF, Babbar Khalsa)
key_commanders_and_units: Army Western Command formations and Punjab Police led by K. P. S. Gill
key_assets_and_platforms: Night-vision devices, bulletproof tractor vehicles, mobile ambush squads
tactical_execution: Nighttime ambushes, continuous vehicle patrols across rural roads, and securing isolated canal tracks where militants operated after dark
outcome_and_strategic_result: Denied militants freedom of movement at night, neutralizing key leaders and ending organized militancy in Punjab by 1994
honors_and_decorations: Extensive gallantry decorations and operational citations

branch: Indian Army, Rashtriya Rifles, and Paramilitary Forces
theater_or_location: Jammu & Kashmir and Punjab
operational_objective: Conduct counter-infiltration along the Line of Control (LoC) and counter-terror operations to maintain law, order, and national integrity
adversary_or_context: Pakistan-sponsored proxy insurgent groups (Hizbul Mujahideen, Lashkar-e-Taiba, Jaish-e-Mohammed)
key_commanders_and_units: XV Corps (Chinar Corps), XVI Corps (White Knight Corps), Rashtriya Rifles (RR) specialized counter-insurgency force
key_assets_and_platforms: Anti-Infiltration Obstacle System (AIOS LoC fence), thermal imagers, drone reconnaissance, bulletproof light vehicles
tactical_execution: Tiered defensive framework: high-altitude forward posts on the LoC, mid-tier village security grids, and targeted surgical cordon-and-search urban operations
outcome_and_strategic_result: Neutralized thousands of foreign and local militants over three decades, securing democratic processes and infrastructure development in J&K
honors_and_decorations: Hundreds of Ashok Chakras, Kirti Chakras, and Shaurya Chakras awarded across decades

branch: Indian Army
theater_or_location: Assam (Brahmaputra Valley)
operational_objective: Neutralize the armed camps of the United Liberation Front of Asom (ULFA) and restore civil administrative control
adversary_or_context: ULFA separatist armed cadres operating from forest bases
key_commanders_and_units: IV Corps; 2 Mountain Division, 5 Mountain Division
key_assets_and_platforms: Riverine gunboats, Mi-17 transport helicopters, light infantry assault squads
tactical_execution: Simultaneous cordon-and-search operations across remote forests of upper Assam, capturing training camps, weapons caches, and financial assets
outcome_and_strategic_result: Weakened ULFA's military wing, forcing key factions to the negotiating table and reducing insurgent attacks on vital oil and tea industries
honors_and_decorations: Sena Medals and Chief of Army Staff commendations

branch: Indian Army (UN Peacekeeping)
theater_or_location: Mogadishu and Baidoa, Somalia
operational_objective: Deliver humanitarian relief, secure supply convoys, disarm rival factional warlords, and protect local civilian populations under a UN mandate
adversary_or_context: Armed Somali warlord militias and irregular clan factions
key_commanders_and_units: Brig. M. P. Bhagat; 66 Mountain Brigade, 7 Bihar, 5 Mahar, 1 JAK LI
key_assets_and_platforms: T-72 tanks, BMP-2 IFVs, Mi-17 helicopters, specialized field medical hospitals
tactical_execution: Secured the volatile Baidoa sector ('City of Death'), guarded food supply corridors, ran free medical camps, and dug water wells while fending off militia ambushes
outcome_and_strategic_result: Successfully stabilized the region with minimal casualties, winning local goodwill and earning praise as one of the best-run UN deployments in Somalia
honors_and_decorations: UN Peacekeeping Medals and international citations

branch: Indian Army supported by IAF and Indian Navy
theater_or_location: Kargil, Dras, Batalik, and Mushkoh sectors (Ladakh, Jammu & Kashmir)
operational_objective: Evict Pakistan Army regular troops (Northern Light Infantry) and irregulars from fortified intrusions on dominant peaks along the Line of Control
adversary_or_context: Pakistan Army elements covertly occupying high-altitude Indian bunkers (Operation Badr)
key_commanders_and_units: Gen. V. P. Malik (COAS), Lt. Gen. H. M. Khanna, Lt. Gen. Kishan Pal; 8 Mountain Division, 3 Mountain Division, 50 Para Brigade
key_assets_and_platforms: 155mm Bofors FH77B howitzers, 122mm Grad multi-barrel rocket launchers, INSAS rifles, specialized snow gear
tactical_execution: Frontal night infantry assaults up sheer vertical cliffs under heavy artillery barrage, recapturing fortified strongpoints at Tololing, Tiger Hill, and Point 4875
outcome_and_strategic_result: Total eviction of Pakistani forces and restoration of the status quo ante along the Line of Control; solidified India's high-altitude tactical dominance
honors_and_decorations: Param Vir Chakra awarded to Capt. Vikram Batra (posthumous), Lt. Manoj Kumar Pandey (posthumous), Grenadier Yogendra Singh Yadav, and Rifleman Sanjay Kumar

branch: Indian Air Force
theater_or_location: Kargil, Batalik, and Dras Heights (J&K)
operational_objective: Provide precision air strikes, close air support, and reconnaissance for Indian ground troops attacking fortified high-altitude Pakistani positions
adversary_or_context: Pakistani entrenched troops armed with man-portable air-defense systems (MANPADS: Stinger, Anza)
key_commanders_and_units: Air Chief Marshal A. Y. Tipnis; Western Air Command squadrons operating from Srinagar, Awantipur, and Adampur
key_assets_and_platforms: Mirage 2000, MiG-27, MiG-21, and MiG-29 fighters, Litening laser designator targeting pods, Paveway laser-guided bombs
tactical_execution: Pioneered high-altitude precision bombing above 30,000 feet outside the reach of shoulder-fired missiles, destroying the main Pakistani logistics hub on Muntho Dhalo and bunker complexes on Tiger Hill
outcome_and_strategic_result: Disrupted enemy logistics and pulverized forward fortifications without crossing the Line of Control, accelerating ground recaptures
honors_and_decorations: Vir Chakra awarded to Sqn. Ldr. Ajay Ahuja (posthumous); multiple gallantry awards to fighter pilots

branch: Indian Navy
theater_or_location: North Arabian Sea (off the coast of Karachi)
operational_objective: Deploy the Western and Eastern naval fleets off the Pakistani coastline to deter naval intervention, prepare a blockade, and support Operation Vijay
adversary_or_context: Pakistan Navy surface and submarine fleet during the Kargil War
key_commanders_and_units: Adm. Sushil Kumar (CNS); Western and Eastern Fleets including carrier battle groups and guided-missile destroyers
key_assets_and_platforms: INS Viraat aircraft carrier, Delhi-class guided-missile destroyers, Rajput-class destroyers, Sindhughosh-class submarines, Sea Harrier jets
tactical_execution: Formed an offensive naval blockade posture along vital maritime trade routes to Karachi, cutting off sea transit lanes and conducting live-firing war drills
outcome_and_strategic_result: Depleted Pakistan's maritime oil and fuel reserves to an estimated six days' supply, exerting strategic pressure that hastened Pakistan's diplomatic retreat from Kargil
honors_and_decorations: Fleet operational readiness citations

branch: Tri-Service (Indian Army, Navy, and Air Force)
theater_or_location: Indo-Pak International Border and the Line of Control
operational_objective: Execute a full-scale military mobilization to pressure Pakistan to cease sponsoring cross-border terrorism following the attack on the Indian Parliament
adversary_or_context: Pakistan Armed Forces mobilizing in counter-deployment positions
key_commanders_and_units: Gen. S. Padmanabhan (COAS); all three Strike Corps (I, II, and XXI Corps) and defensive field formations
key_assets_and_platforms: T-90S and T-72 tanks, heavy artillery, fighter squadrons, forward naval strike fleets
tactical_execution: Nearly 500,000 troops moved to battle stations along the western border, mined forward corridors, and deployed combat air patrols for a 10-month standoff
outcome_and_strategic_result: Compelled Pakistani President Pervez Musharraf to deliver his January 2002 address pledging not to let Pakistani territory be used for cross-border terror; exposed mobilization delays that led to the development of the Cold Start Doctrine
honors_and_decorations: Operation Parakram Medal awarded to all deployed personnel

branch: Indian Army
theater_or_location: Hil Kaka mountain ridge, Surankote, Poonch district (Jammu & Kashmir)
operational_objective: Dismantle an extensive fortified insurgent logistics hub and bunker base built in the dense forests south of the Pir Panjal range
adversary_or_context: Over 100 foreign and local terrorists belonging to Lashkar-e-Taiba, Jaish-e-Mohammed, and Harkat-ul-Jihad-al-Islami
key_commanders_and_units: Maj. Gen. Hardev Lidder; 9 Para SF, 163 Brigade, Rashtriya Rifles units
key_assets_and_platforms: Lancer attack helicopters, thermal sensors, directional radar, infantry mountain assault weaponry
tactical_execution: Encircled the Hil Kaka mountain heights in snowy conditions, using air-landed special forces and heavy mortar fire to systematically clear interconnected bunker systems
outcome_and_strategic_result: Over 64 terrorists killed and massive quantities of arms, satellite phones, and rations seized, neutralizing the primary terrorist transit hub south of the Pir Panjal
honors_and_decorations: Multiple Shaurya Chakras and Sena Medals awarded for high-altitude counter-terror operations

operation_name: Operation Rainbow, Castor & Madath (Indian Ocean Tsunami Relief)
branch: Tri-Service (Navy, Air Force, and Army)
theater_or_location: Andaman & Nicobar Islands, Sri Lanka, Maldives, and Indonesia
operational_objective: Deliver emergency humanitarian aid, medical assistance, and search-and-rescue operations following the catastrophic Indian Ocean Tsunami
adversary_or_context: Humanitarian Disaster (9.1 magnitude mega-thrust earthquake and resulting tsunami)
key_commanders_and_units: Integrated Defence Staff (IDS), Eastern and Southern Naval Commands
key_assets_and_platforms: 40+ Indian Navy warships (hospital ships, survey vessels), IL-76 and An-32 transport aircraft, Mi-17 and Chetak helicopters
tactical_execution: Simultaneously handled domestic relief across Tamil Nadu and the devastated Andaman and Nicobar Islands while deploying naval task forces to provide food, clean water, and field hospitals to Sri Lanka, the Maldives, and Banda Aceh
outcome_and_strategic_result: Saved thousands of lives across the region; demonstrated blue-water disaster response capabilities and established India's standing as a leading regional net security provider
honors_and_decorations: Global humanitarian commendations from the UN and affected regional states

branch: Indian Navy supported by Indian Air Force
theater_or_location: Beirut Port, Lebanon to Larnaca, Cyprus (Mediterranean Sea)
operational_objective: Evacuate Indian, Nepalese, Sri Lankan, and Lebanese-origin citizens trapped in the conflict zone during the 2006 Lebanon War
adversary_or_context: Armed conflict between Israel Defense Forces and Hezbollah, with Israeli airstrikes targeting Lebanese ports and roads
key_commanders_and_units: Rear Adm. Anup Singh (Western Fleet Commander); Task Force comprising INS Mumbai, INS Betwa, INS Brahmaputra, INS Shakti
key_assets_and_platforms: Guided-missile destroyers, frigates, fleet replenishment tankers, Sea King helicopters, Air India charter aircraft
tactical_execution: Naval task force diverted from Mediterranean exercises into Beirut harbor during a temporary ceasefire, embarking nearly 2,300 evacuees and ferrying them safely to Cyprus for airlift back to India
outcome_and_strategic_result: One of the largest overseas naval evacuation operations conducted since World War II, executed with zero casualties
honors_and_decorations: Praise from international governments for evacuating foreign nationals from danger

branch: National Security Guard (NSG) and Indian Navy (MARCOS)
theater_or_location: Taj Mahal Palace Hotel, Oberoi Trident, and Nariman House, Mumbai
operational_objective: Neutralize Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists holding hostages across multiple urban landmarks and secure civilian lives during the 26/11 attacks
adversary_or_context: Ten heavily armed, fidayeen terrorists carrying AK-47s, grenades, and RDX explosives
key_commanders_and_units: J. K. Dutt (DG NSG); 51 Special Action Group (SAG), Marine Commandos (MARCOS)
key_assets_and_platforms: Mi-17 helicopters for slithering drops, corner-shot weapons, MP5 submachine guns, explosive entry equipment
tactical_execution: Room-to-room clearing of heritage hotels and a heliborne assault onto the roof of Nariman House, methodically rescuing hundreds of trapped guests while drawing and neutralizing terrorist fire
outcome_and_strategic_result: Nine terrorists were eliminated and one captured alive (Ajmal Kasab); spurred national security overhauls, leading to the creation of the National Investigation Agency (NIA) and regional NSG operational hubs
honors_and_decorations: Ashok Chakra awarded posthumously to Major Sandeep Unnikrishnan and Havildar Gajender Singh

branch: Joint (Indian Air Force, Indian Army, NDRF, and ITBP)
theater_or_location: Kedarnath, Badrinath, and Mandakini Valley (Uttarakhand)
operational_objective: Rescue over 100,000 pilgrims, tourists, and locals stranded in mountainous terrain following flash floods and cloudbursts
adversary_or_context: Humanitarian disaster caused by Himalayan cloudbursts, severe landslides, and washed-out roads
key_commanders_and_units: Air Marshal S. B. Deo; Central Air Command, Western Command, Army Surya Command (Operation Surya Hope)
key_assets_and_platforms: Mi-17 V5, ALH Dhruv, Cheetah helicopters, C-130J Super Hercules transports
tactical_execution: Flew more than 3,500 sorties in narrow, fog-covered valleys, landing on makeshift helipads to evacuate stranded survivors and drop emergency rations
outcome_and_strategic_result: Successfully rescued more than 20,000 people by air and over 80,000 by foot bridges built by Army engineers; largest civilian helicopter-borne rescue mission in aviation history
honors_and_decorations: Shaurya Chakra awarded to IAF and ITBP rescue personnel who lost their lives in a crash during rescue operations

branch: Joint (Indian Navy, Indian Air Force, and Ministry of External Affairs)
theater_or_location: Aden, Al-Hudaydah, and Sana'a (Yemen) via Djibouti
operational_objective: Evacuate Indian nationals and foreign citizens from Yemen during the active civil war and foreign military intervention
adversary_or_context: Active urban conflict between Houthi rebels and Saudi-led coalition air and ground strikes
key_commanders_and_units: Gen. (Retd) V. K. Singh (MoS External Affairs on site); INS Mumbai, INS Tarkash, INS Sumitra, IAF No. 81 Squadron
key_assets_and_platforms: Guided-missile destroyers, stealth frigates, C-17 Globemaster III heavy airlifters, Air India planes
tactical_execution: Naval warships entered bombarded, unlit ports at Aden and Al-Hudaydah to embark evacuees under sniper fire, while C-17 airlifters flew sorties out of Sana'a airport to Djibouti
outcome_and_strategic_result: Evacuated 4,640 Indian citizens and 961 foreign nationals from 41 countries with zero casualties, winning global diplomatic praise
honors_and_decorations: International diplomatic acclaim and Nao Sena Medals for ship commanding officers

branch: Indian Army
theater_or_location: India-Myanmar border (Sagaing Division inside Myanmar)
operational_objective: Target and destroy camps of northeast militant outfits that had ambushed and killed 18 soldiers of the 6 Dogra regiment in Chandel, Manipur
adversary_or_context: NSCN-Khaplang (NSCN-K) and KYKL insurgent groups sheltering across the international border
key_commanders_and_units: Lt. Gen. Bipin Rawat (GOC III Corps); 21 Para Special Forces
key_assets_and_platforms: Dhruv ALH and Mi-17 helicopters, specialized assault carbines, thermal imaging scopes
tactical_execution: Para SF commandos inserted near the border crossed into Myanmar under cover of darkness, attacked two insurgent training camps with assault weapons, and exfiltrated cleanly
outcome_and_strategic_result: Eliminated dozens of armed insurgents without Indian casualties, establishing a precedent for cross-border retaliatory strikes against hostile sanctuaries
honors_and_decorations: Kirti Chakras and Shaurya Chakras awarded to participating Para SF commandos

branch: Indian Army (Special Forces)
theater_or_location: Across the Line of Control, Pakistan-administered Jammu & Kashmir
operational_objective: Destroy terrorist launch pads along the LoC preparing to infiltrate into India following the Uri terror attack on an Army base
adversary_or_context: Multiple terrorist launch pads operated by Jaish-e-Mohammed and Lashkar-e-Taiba with Pakistan Army border post support
key_commanders_and_units: Lt. Gen. D. S. Hooda (Northern Command); 4 Para SF and 9 Para SF teams
key_assets_and_platforms: Tavor TAR-21 assault rifles, Carl Gustaf rocket launchers, thermal imaging weapon sights, night-vision equipment
tactical_execution: Multi-team foot incursions across the LoC into Pakistan-administered territory, simultaneous precision missile and rocket strikes on five terror launch pads, and clean exfiltration before dawn
outcome_and_strategic_result: Significant terrorist casualties and destruction of launch infrastructure; represented a major shift in India's strategic policy toward cross-border retaliatory deterrence
honors_and_decorations: Kirti Chakra awarded to assault leaders and multiple Shaurya Chakras to team members

branch: Indian Air Force
theater_or_location: Balakot, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, Pakistan
operational_objective: Conduct a non-military, pre-emptive air strike against the primary training camp of Jaish-e-Mohammed in retaliation for the Pulwama suicide bombing
adversary_or_context: Jaish-e-Mohammed high-level training facility on Jabba Top hill and Pakistan Air Force air defenses
key_commanders_and_units: Air Chief Marshal B. S. Dhanoa; No. 1 Squadron ('The Tigers') and No. 7 Squadron ('Battle Axes')
key_assets_and_platforms: Mirage 2000 multi-role jets carrying SPICE-2000 precision-guided penetrator bombs, Netra AEW&C aircraft, Su-30MKI escorts
tactical_execution: Staged diversionary sweeps along the border while a strike package of Mirage 2000s penetrated deep into Pakistani airspace at Balakot, releasing bunker-penetrating precision bombs onto target buildings before returning safely
outcome_and_strategic_result: First air strike into sovereign Pakistani territory outside J&K since the 1971 war, establishing a new strategic deterrence threshold against cross-border terror acts
honors_and_decorations: Yudh Seva Medals and Vayu Sena Medals awarded to participating pilots; Vir Chakra awarded to Wing Cdr. Abhinandan Varthaman during the aerial skirmish the following day

branch: Indian Army
theater_or_location: Kailash Range, South of Pangong Tso (Eastern Ladakh)
operational_objective: Pre-emptively occupy tactically dominant mountain peaks along the Kailash Range to gain observation over Chinese PLA positions amid the 2020 Ladakh standoff
adversary_or_context: Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) Ground Forces encroaching on friction points in Eastern Ladakh
key_commanders_and_units: Lt. Gen. Y. K. Joshi (Northern Command); Special Frontier Force (SFF / Vikas Battalion), Ladakh Scouts, 14 Corps
key_assets_and_platforms: T-90 Bhishma and T-72 tanks hauled to extreme altitudes, BMP-2 IFVs, thermal imaging reconnaissance arrays
tactical_execution: Stealth night climb to occupy dominant heights along the Kailash Range, including Magar Hill, Gurung Hill, Rechin La, and Rezang La, positioning armor on high ridges overlooking the PLA Spanggur Gap base
outcome_and_strategic_result: Gave India decisive tactical leverage over Chinese positions, which facilitated negotiated disengagements from Pangong Tso, Galwan, and the Gogra-Hot Springs friction areas
honors_and_decorations: Maha Vir Chakra awarded to Col. B. Santosh Babu (posthumously for Galwan defense); Sena Medals to SFF personnel

branch: Joint (Indian Air Force, Indian Army, and Ministry of External Affairs)
theater_or_location: Hamid Karzai International Airport, Kabul, Afghanistan
operational_objective: Evacuate Indian diplomats, citizens, Afghan Hindu and Sikh minorities, and foreign nationals from Kabul following the Taliban's takeover of Afghanistan
adversary_or_context: Collapse of the Afghan government, Taliban siege of Kabul, and active suicide-bomb threats by ISIS-K around the airport perimeter
key_commanders_and_units: No. 81 Squadron IAF; C-17 Globemaster and C-130J transport crews; Indian Air Force Garuda Special Forces providing perimeter security
key_assets_and_platforms: C-17 Globemaster III heavy airlifters, C-130J Super Hercules tactical transports, Air India charter aircraft
tactical_execution: Flew tactical combat landings and takeoffs through chaotic airspace without civil air traffic control, using Garuda commandos to secure passengers through crowded airport gates
outcome_and_strategic_result: Evacuated nearly 700 individuals, including Afghan minority leaders and sacred Guru Granth Sahib swaroops, without casualties amid terrorist bombings nearby
honors_and_decorations: Vayu Sena Medals and Chief of Air Staff Commendation Cards awarded to aircrews

branch: Indian Air Force and Commercial Aviation (Civil-Military Coordination)
theater_or_location: Ukraine border states (Romania, Poland, Hungary, and Slovakia)
operational_objective: Evacuate Indian students and citizens stranded across Ukraine following the outbreak of the Russian invasion of Ukraine
adversary_or_context: War zone logistics breakdown, missile strikes, and active urban combat in Ukrainian cities (Kyiv, Kharkiv, Sumy)
key_commanders_and_units: Four Union Special Envoys stationed on European borders; IAF No. 81 Squadron (C-17s) alongside commercial airlines
key_assets_and_platforms: Boeing C-17 Globemaster III heavy military transport aircraft, civilian passenger airliners, consular border coordination cells
tactical_execution: Coordinated humanitarian border transit corridors out of besieged cities like Sumy and Kharkiv, transporting students across international borders for direct airlift to India
outcome_and_strategic_result: Evacuated over 22,500 Indian citizens and scores of foreign nationals via 90 dedicated flights, demonstrating India's diplomatic leverage and emergency logistical capabilities
honors_and_decorations: National recognition for coordinated civil-military overseas evacuation and disaster management
